title: CloudFront 4xx/5xx Error Rate Spike

compliance.assurance_rationale: Saved search evidence for SI-4 when alert outputs are archived.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudfront:accesslogs` events with `sc_status>=400` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.155 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudfront:accesslogs` traffic without `sc_status>=400`. Confirm UC-4.1.155 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudfront:accesslogs` collected via Splunk Add-on for AWS (`Splunk_TA_aws`, Splunkbase 1876); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

description: UC-4.1.155 — CloudFront 4xx/5xx Error Rate Spike: queries AWS `aws:cloudfront:accesslogs` for search criteria `sc_status>=400` and returns actor, resource, and region context for availability review and change validation.
value: At the AWS edge, 'CloudFront 4xx/5xx Error Rate Spike' request anomalies may indicate scraping, credential stuffing, or WAF bypass attempts before origin servers are overwhelmed. UC-4.1.155 drives medium-priority availability alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Enable cloudfront integration in AWS and forward findings/logs via `Splunk_TA_aws` into `index=aws` with `sourcetype=aws:cloudfront:accesslogs`. Validate field extractions before alerting.
visualization: Notable-style table, severity timeline, single-value open finding count.
knownFalsePositives: Approved change windows; documented automation service principals; sandbox accounts excluded via lookup.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Splunk Add-on for AWS (`Splunk_TA_aws`, Splunkbase 1876) with the modular input for `aws:cloudfront:accesslogs`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `cs_uri_stem` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable cloudfront integration in AWS and forward findings/logs via `Splunk_TA_aws` into `index=aws` with `sourcetype=aws:cloudfront:accesslogs`. Validate field extractions before alerting.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudfront:accesslogs" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudfront:accesslogs" sc_status>=400
| table _time cs_uri_stem sc_status cs_method x_edge_location
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.155_cloudfront_4xx_5xx_error_155"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudfront:accesslogs` in `index=aws` to detect cloudfront 4xx/5xx error rate spike. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the CloudFront console Reports and analytics for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `cs_uri_stem` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_155_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Notable-style table, severity timeline, single-value open finding count..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Add-on for AWS (`Splunk_TA_aws`, Splunkbase 1876) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloudfront 4xx/5xx error rate spike so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
